reason: The speed numbers are exactly what I care about and I'd install it to test on my own RAW folders, but I won't hand my culling workflow to one developer on version 0.4. If it vanishes in a year I'd have to re-learn everything.
why_switch_or_not: Rapid next x5 in about 85 ms against 600-900 ms for FastStone would be a real difference when I'm culling hundreds of RAW+JPG frames, and showing RAW and JPG as separate pictures is how I want it. But nobody has told me how it handles my 40 MP RAW files, how culling works (rating, marking, moving rejects), or that it has a proper full-screen mode like FastStone's. Nothing in the description says it reads cbz comfortably as a manga reader, only that it opens zip/cbz archives. I'd keep FastStone as the default until I have tested it on my own cards.
current_app_pros: FastStone's full-screen mode with the hover toolbars, the browser with thumbnails, and the simple editor all in one program. I know every shortcut and have used it for years. It opens zip/cbz and my RAW files well enough.
current_app_pains: It is slow when I hammer next through big RAW or JPG folders, with a visible lag of 600+ ms across several quick presses. The development is slow too, and a few formats fail.
objection: One developer, version 0.4: will it still be maintained next year? I'm not moving my whole culling routine onto a project that may be abandoned.
would_change_my_mind: A month of using it on a real shoot with no crashes, plus clear culling features (ratings, marks, move/delete rejects) and a visible update history showing it is being kept up.
